svg.title: Proof. If all integer square samples of a sum of components through degree k vanish, multiply the rescaled component of degree lby tk−land choose integer xt with txt →x; the finite sum is zero for t > 0, and continuity at t = 0 leaves only N(k) ij (x, 0). The top curl vanishes, so by Theorem 16.1 the top potential vanishes, and descending induction removes all components. Among kernels of finite sampling families choose one of minimal dimension; appending any slot cannot lower it, so a vector in it is killed by every slot and is zero. For C, equip Y with the sum of invariant color inner products; the range of T is invariant, its orthogonal projection commutes with the adjoint action, and C is that projection followed by T −1 on the range. No invariant inner product on X is needed.
